technical_and_design_decisions: The implementation will be done in Go, as it is the primary language for Hyperledger Fabric.
Functions will be added to a dedicated channel configuration package (e.g., `channelconfig` or a new fit-for-purpose library package) to ensure modularity.

ConfigUpdate transactions will be computed using standard Fabric protobuf definitions and existing utility functions where possible.

Effort estimates are in work-hours and represent the most likely duration for a single developer.

activities.activity_description: Define the API signatures, input/output types, and overall design for the new channel configuration library functions.
Implement functions to add and remove orderer endpoints from an orderer org's config group, and compute the resulting ConfigUpdate transaction (U1, U2).
Implement a function to retrieve existing policies for a specific organization without manual parsing (U3).
Implement a function to retrieve existing orderer, application, and channel capabilities from a config transaction (U4).
Implement toggle functions to add and remove application, orderer, and channel capabilities (U5).
Implement a function to retrieve existing application configuration returning a config.Application object (U6).
Implement functions to add and remove ACLs from an application group's configuration (U7).
Split the existing giant end-to-end example test into smaller, varied examples covering orderer config, app values, org management, MSP modifications, and capabilities (U8).
Write and execute unit tests for all new functions and ensure integration with the existing Fabric configuration workflow.
